Definition: neuter of a derivative of ἕρπω (to creep); a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare H7431)) a small animal:--creeping thing, serpent.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says herpetón, it means creeping thing, serpent. The word appears 4 times, and in Acts, Romans, and James it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: herpetón matters to me because even the creeping things belong to God, and He showed Peter they were clean. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
